title: Restore the repair café record
instructions: Read the complete passage first. Enter exactly one word in each gap. Use evidence from neighbouring sentences to preserve reference, contrast and chronology.

parts.prompt: Gap 1: identify who arrived first by linking the earlier roles with the following pronoun and toolkit reference.

response.rationale: The following sentence uses “He” and mentions a toolkit, while the opening role sentence assigns electrical examination to Farid. Together those cross-sentence clues identify Farid.

parts.hint: Follow “He” and the toolkit back to the two organisers and their different roles.
parts.correct_explanation: Farid is the male organiser responsible for examining devices, so the later pronoun and toolkit reference continue his identity chain.

parts.prompt: Gap 2: use a demonstrative that refers to the whole successful lamp repair in the previous sentence.

response.rationale: Both “This” and “That” can point back to the complete event in which Farid repaired the switch and the lamp lit, making that success the cause of the visitors' confidence.

parts.hint: The missing word points back to the complete successful event, not merely to the lamp.
parts.correct_explanation: “This” refers to the whole successful repair; “That” is also an explicitly accepted demonstrative here.

parts.prompt: Gap 3: signal the contrast between the organisers' expectation and the difficult radio that actually arrived next.

response.rationale: The difficult radio conflicts with the expectation of mostly simple repairs. “However”, “Yet” and “Instead” can all mark that contrast in this position.

parts.hint: The next repair differs from what the organisers expected.
parts.correct_explanation: “However” marks the contrast between the expected simple work and the difficult radio; “Yet” and “Instead” are approved alternatives.

parts.prompt: Gap 4: complete the inversion “Only ___ did he notice” by following the earlier sequence of tests.

response.rationale: Farid notices the loose connection after testing the battery, speaker and wires. “Only then did he notice” links the discovery to that preceding sequence and correctly triggers inversion.

parts.hint: The discovery happens after all the tests described in the previous sentence.
parts.correct_explanation: “Then” places the discovery after the preceding tests and completes the inverted structure “Only then did he notice”.

parts.prompt: Gap 5: use a plural object pronoun that refers to the lamp owners named in the previous sentence.

response.rationale: The antecedent is the plural human noun phrase “The owners of the lamps”. After “to”, the required object pronoun is “them”.

parts.hint: Rina returns the lamps to their two owners.
parts.correct_explanation: “Them” is the plural object pronoun that continues the reference to the lamp owners.

parts.prompt: Gap 6: show that Farid repeated the action after the first unsuccessful attempt.

response.rationale: The earlier sentence states that Farid already switched the radio on once. “Again” marks the later switch as a repeated action after he adjusted the connection.

parts.hint: Find the same switching action earlier in the paragraph.
parts.correct_explanation: “Again” links the successful second switch to the earlier unsuccessful attempt.

parts.prompt: Gap 7: use the possessive determiner that continues the reference to Mr Lee.

response.rationale: Mr Lee is the singular male person who stays to help. The possessive determiner before “help” must therefore be “his”.

parts.hint: The help comes from Mr Lee in the previous sentence.
parts.correct_explanation: “His” links the helpful action back to Mr Lee and correctly modifies the noun “help”.

parts.prompt: Gap 8: use a singular object pronoun that refers to the shared notebook in the previous sentence.

response.rationale: The singular object being studied is the shared notebook. The object pronoun “it” continues that reference without unnecessarily repeating the noun.

parts.hint: New volunteers will study the object Rina used to record every fault and solution.
parts.correct_explanation: “It” refers back to the singular shared notebook and completes the reference chain.
